delete.description: Delete a config-defined agent from the instance agent store, and clear `default_agent` when it pointed at that agent. Takes effect fully on the next serve boot. The instance's governing agent (`nova`) cannot be removed and returns 400.

schema.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned as cursor.previous or cursor.next in the previous response.

get.description: Retrieve sessions in the requested order. Items keep that order across pages; use cursor.next or cursor.previous to move through the ordered list.

post.description: Create a session at the requested location.

put.description: Replace the chat's tag set — tags organize chat processes; tag a root to organize its thread tree.

get.description: The instance-wide tag map: session id → tags. The client store's bootstrap source.

post.description: Attach a viewer, say 'still here', take over control, or detach. Returns the session's whole presence snapshot; every attached surface also receives it as `session.presence.updated`.

get.description: Sessions with someone attached right now: session id → presence. The client store's bootstrap source; sessions absent from the result are unattended. This instance answers only for its OWN sessions — it is not a directory of who is online.
Retrieve foreground Session drains currently owned by this NovaClaw process. Sessions absent from the result are inactive.
List durable execution and recovery state, including paused failures and their human-readable details. Pass sessionID to inspect one session without transferring the whole ledger.
What this session's current attempt declared and what it checked: the frozen plan, each quality check that ran with its command and exit code, and any spawned children.
Retrieve a session by ID.

patch.description: Rename a session, replace its metadata, archive it, or set/remove its Device pin; returns the updated record.

delete.description: Permanently delete a session and its descendants (messages, todos, tags cascade).

get.description: Retrieve the sessions forked or spawned from the given parent session.

Resolve a session's effective configuration by walking its parent chain root-ward (undefined = inherit), and report which ancestor supplied each field. Covers the SessionConfig fields only: the saved permission ruleset does not resolve through this walk, the reported permissionMode is the config-walk result before auto-mode grants and the unattended stance narrow it further, and systemPromptOverride is the per-session override rather than the composed system prompt.

post.description: Clone a session's transcript into a fresh session, optionally truncated at (and excluding) a message.

get.description: Inputs admitted for this session that the runner has not promoted into the transcript yet, oldest first. A prompt sent mid-turn waits here until the current step finishes; it is never dropped.
get.summary: Queued prompts not yet read by the agent

get.description: Retrieve the todo list the session's agent maintains.

post.description: Switch the agent used by subsequent provider turns. Refuses with 409 when that colleague already has a chat — a colleague has exactly one.
Switch the model used by subsequent provider turns.
Take control (operator) so Nova stops auto-responding, or hand back (nova) so it resumes and drains queued input.

get.description: The session's current working folder, plus the folder it was created in when that one has gone missing and the session was degraded into a scratch folder. `missing` is what lets a client offer to repoint: without it the substitution is only visible as a one-off notice in the transcript, which a reader who returns later has already scrolled past.
get.summary: Where a session is working, and what it lost

post.description: Move this session's working folder. Written through the `working_folder` session component, so it re-derives project identity, publishes the same Moved event an agent's own move would, and clears any recorded missing-folder recovery. Exists because a folder that moved is something the USER knows and the agent does not: when a working folder disappears the session degrades into a scratch folder and keeps running, and only a person can say where the real one went.
post.summary: Point a session at a different working folder

post.description: Change the permission mode mid-session; the MODE_RULES overlay applies from the next turn.
Enable/disable Strict mode for this session and set its racing attempts + time budget; null clears the override back to inherit (parent chain, then global config). Applies from the next turn.
Enable/disable one harness feature for this session; null clears the override back to inherit (parent chain, then global config). Applies from the next turn.
post.summary: Set a per-session harness-feature override (introspection · quality · affective · thinkingBudget)

post.description: Switch this chat between interactive and the unattended types (auto-prompting · goal-oriented). Attendance derives from the chain root's type: an unattended chat is CONFINED rather than permissive: out-of-folder writes are DENIED outright instead of parked as an ask nobody can answer, and bash is confined by the Agent Jail (denied outright where no jail backend exists). Applies immediately.
post.summary: Set the session's kernel thread type (Mode)

post.description: Replace this session's system-prompt override (composed after the persona baseline, before the agent prompt); null clears it. Children and forks inherit through the config walk. Applies from the next turn.
post.summary: Set the session's system-prompt override layer

post.description: Run one shell command to completion against the session's location; the transcript renders from the durable shell events (no model turn).
Expand and dispatch a slash command: a prompt-kind command runs a turn on this session; a subtask command spawns a child session (surfaced via session events).
Durably admit one session input and schedule agent-loop execution unless resume is false.
Compact a session conversation.
Block until the session completes via exit() (its result is recorded). Times out after ~10 minutes with 503 — re-call to continue waiting.
Stage or move a reversible session boundary and optionally apply its file changes.

get.description: Retrieve the active context messages for a session (all messages after the last compaction).
Read one finite page of public durable Session events after an exclusive aggregate sequence. Newly committed events may appear on later pages.
Replay durable events after an aggregate sequence, then continue with new durable events.

post.description: Interrupt active execution owned by this NovaClaw process. Idle interruption is a no-op.
Record explicit operator authority, reset the recovery circuit breaker, and resume queued work without requiring a model response.

get.description: Retrieve one projected message owned by the Session.

post.description: Render the whole session to a Markdown file inside the session's own project folder. The destination is relative to that folder and never replaces an existing file — a name collision is written alongside it, and the response says where the bytes actually landed. A session that is still running exports what exists so far and is marked as captured mid-turn.

directory.description: Folder to write the .md into, relative to the session's own project folder. Omitted = that folder itself. An absolute path, or one that resolves outside the project, is refused.

filename.description: File name to write. Omitted = derived from the session title. Basename only.

schema.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned as cursor.previous or cursor.next in the previous response. Do not combine with order.

get.description: Retrieve projected messages for a session. Items keep the requested order across pages; use cursor.next or cursor.previous to move through the ordered timeline.
Retrieve available models ordered by release date.
Retrieve active AI providers so clients can show provider availability and configuration.
List tested laptop-friendly models, live resource preflight, verified-download progress and managed llama.cpp status.

post.description: Start a resumable verified background installation. The instance-owned llama.cpp server remains stopped until this model receives a prompt.
Stop an active managed-model install or unload the instance-owned llama.cpp model.

get.description: Retrieve a single AI provider so clients can inspect its availability and endpoint settings.

delete.description: Delete a config-defined provider from the instance catalog store (T10iv: a true key delete, not a disable-list hide). Takes effect fully on the next serve boot.

Delete a single model from a provider in the instance catalog store, keeping the provider itself (and so its endpoint URL, auth and request defaults). Instance-wide and durable. A model that is in no layer is a 404, never a cheerful 204.

get.description: Retrieve available integrations and their authentication methods.
Retrieve one integration and its authentication methods.

post.description: Run a key authentication method and store the resulting credential.
Start an OAuth attempt and return the authorization details.

get.description: Poll the current status of an OAuth attempt.

delete.description: Cancel an OAuth attempt and release its resources.

post.description: Complete a code-based OAuth attempt and store the resulting credential.

delete.description: Remove a stored integration credential.

get.description: Report malformed stored secrets and supported account or identity repair actions.
Retrieve the installed messenger platform drivers and their capabilities.
Retrieve every configured messenger account with its live connection status.

post.description: Configure a messenger account for an installed driver. The optional secret (bot token, API key) is stored in the credential store and never returned.

patch.description: Update a messenger account's label, enabled state, settings, or stored secret.

delete.description: Remove a messenger account, its stored credential, seen chats, contacts, bindings, and cursor.

post.description: Mint a single-use, 10-minute pairing code. A remote sender redeems it with /pair <code> in a DM to become a paired contact at the chosen trust.

get.description: The account's known chats — the live driver list where the platform allows enumeration (seeding the seen-cache), else the seen-cache. `ok:false` carries a plain-words reason (not connected, nothing seen yet).
Every live session↔chat binding on this instance, with the chat's human title from the seen-cache where known.

post.description: Link a session to a remote chat at an explicit trust tier (operator | client | audience — always user-chosen, never inferred). One session per chat: if the chat is already bound the call fails naming the holding session; pass steal:true to rebind deliberately.
post.summary: Bind a session to a chat

delete.description: Remove a session↔chat binding. The chat stops driving (or reporting to) the session immediately.

post.description: Start a login-auth attempt for an account whose driver signs into the user's own messenger account (inputs answer the driver's loginPrompts — e.g. phone and optional 2FA password). The provider sends a confirmation code; complete the attempt with it.

get.description: Retrieve the state of a pending or recently finished messenger login attempt, including the step's CURRENT instructions and scannable image — poll this while an attempt is pending, because providers may rotate what the user must act on (WhatsApp mints a fresh linked-device QR every ~20s).

delete.description: Abandon a pending messenger login attempt and release its resources.

post.description: Finish a login attempt with the confirmation code the provider sent. On success the session credential is stored and the account reconnects; a mistyped code keeps the attempt pending (error kind messenger_login_retry).

get.description: Retrieve every scheduled agent-launch task with its next-fire time.

post.description: Schedule a repeatable or one-shot agent launch. The recurrence is structured (once/daily/weekly/monthly/yearly); the fired session runs the given prompt.

patch.description: Patch a scheduled agent-launch task — pause/resume it (enabled), or change its title, prompt, recurrence, model, folder, or permission mode. The next-fire time is recomputed; a disabled schedule has none.

delete.description: Delete a scheduled agent-launch task by id.

get.description: Recent scheduled-launch fires across all schedules, newest first (the run history).
Every recipe on this install, name-sorted. `builtin` marks the ones NovaClaw shipped.

post.description: Writes recipe.md. Omit `slug` to derive it from the name; pass it to update in place.

patch.description: Edits the requested lines inside the author's own bytes: line endings, a BOM, unknown frontmatter keys, key order and the trailing newline all survive. Use this rather than a save when you are changing one field — a save takes the whole recipe.
patch.summary: Change some of a recipe's fields and nothing else

delete.summary: Delete a recipe and its assets

get.description: The bytes of recipe.md exactly as they are on disk — the readable part of the folder — plus the host-capability facts it declares checked against THIS machine, the artifacts a finished cook should leave, and the shelf it is on. Read-only: the capability probe resolves names on PATH and stats paths, and never runs a candidate.
get.summary: Read a recipe's file, and what it needs and produces

post.description: Writes the supplied file byte for byte under a free slug — never overwriting an existing recipe. This paste convenience is explicitly asset-free; use the ZIP import for a complete folder.
post.summary: Store pasted recipe markdown without assets

get.description: Returns a standard ZIP containing recipe.md and every nested binary or text asset.

post.description: Validates a bounded standard ZIP, reserves a free slug, and commits recipe.md plus its asset tree atomically.
Copies the folder and its assets under a free slug — the 'make it mine' move for a shipped recipe.
Copies the recipe's assets into a work directory and starts a session there with the recipe as its prompt. The recipe itself is never modified, so it stays re-runnable.

Reads the work directory and reports, per artifact the recipe declares, whether it is there and whether it is the shape its name implies. Deterministic and read-only: the harness looks at the filesystem, so the verdict does not depend on what the model said about its own work. Runs nothing and writes nothing, and may be called as often as you like.
post.summary: Check what a cook actually produced

delete.description: Delete a contributed home-app manifest by id. Built-in tiles are not manifests and are unaffected; deleting an id that does not exist succeeds, so the call is idempotent.

get.description: Retrieve saved permissions, optionally filtered by project.

delete.description: Remove a saved permission by ID.

post.description: Evaluate the effective permission rules for a session action.

get.description: Serve one file relative to the requested location. A browser download presents a `ticket` from `fs.readToken` in place of the `Authorization` header it cannot set.

post.description: Create a short-lived single-use ticket authorizing one browser download of one file.

get.description: Read one file exactly as it existed in a captured session revision.
List direct children of one directory relative to the requested location.
Find recursively ranked filesystem entries relative to the requested location.
List direct file and folder names without booting a project or agent location for the directory.
Retrieve currently registered commands.

delete.description: Delete a config-defined command from the instance command store. Takes effect fully on the next serve boot.

get.description: Retrieve version control information for a location, such as its branch and default branch.
Retrieve the changed files in the working tree, with counts and no patches.
Retrieve the diff for the working tree (mode=git) or against the default branch (mode=branch).
Retrieve a raw patch of the uncommitted changes, as text a patch tool can apply directly.

post.description: Apply a raw patch to the working tree. Fails with kind 'non-git' outside a repository and 'not-clean' when the tree has changes.

get.description: Scan the location's own manifests and propose check, typecheck, test and lint commands, with the evidence for each. Proposes only: nothing is run and nothing is saved.
Retrieve currently registered skills.
Subscribe to native event payloads for the server.
List shells available for human terminal sessions on this NovaClaw instance.
List PTY sessions for a location, including exited sessions retained until removal.

post.description: Create a pseudo-terminal session for a location.

delete.description: Terminate and remove every PTY session for a location.

get.description: Get one PTY session, including its exit code once exited.

put.description: Update the title or viewport size of one PTY session.

delete.description: Terminate and remove one PTY session.

get.description: Report whether a running terminal shell has descendant processes before a destructive close.

post.description: Create a short-lived single-use ticket for opening a PTY WebSocket connection.

get.description: Establish a WebSocket connection streaming PTY output and accepting terminal input.
List PTY sessions across every active location owned by one instance directory.

delete.description: Terminate every PTY session across active locations owned by one instance directory.

get.description: List references available in the requested location.

delete.description: Delete a config-defined reference alias from the instance reference store. Takes effect fully on the next serve boot.

post.description: Delete one or more values from the instance configuration by path. `PATCH /config` merges and can never remove a key; this is the deletion verb. Instance-wide, applied in one transaction, and live without a restart. A path that names nothing is a 400 and NOTHING is removed.

Read `novaclaw.log` — the instance's keyed, rotated activity log — filtered and rendered server-side. The instance's own log directory is the only source; there is no path parameter. The response carries the rendered text and nothing structured, so there is exactly one renderer of a log line in the product.
Streams this instance's own recent activity log through the maintenance-plane projection. The source is fixed server-side; the request accepts no filesystem path.
post.summary: Stream bounded diagnostics from this instance

get.description: Show every live refusal, the exact synthetic payload the sender would produce, and its generated field disclosure.

status.description: Task status; any string. Canonical: pending, in_progress, completed, cancelled.

priority.description: Task priority; any string. Canonical: high, medium, low.

startCommand.description: Additional startup script to run after the project's start command

paths.description: The paths to remove. Applied all-or-nothing: if any one names nothing, none are removed.

cleared.description: Default refs cleared because they pointed at something removed (`model`, `default_agent`). A dangling default reads as configured and resolves to nothing, so it is pruned with its target.

text.description: The matching lines, oldest first, already rendered for the requested plane. Display it; do not re-derive it — the server owns the one rendering.

scanned.description: Lines examined. 0 with no lines means an empty or absent log.

truncated.description: The scan ceiling stopped the walk, so older history was not examined.

hook.description: A closed, harness-owned event selector. Free-form code is never executed.

formatter.description: Enable built-in formatters or configure formatter overrides

name.description: Tool name (lowercase slug) listed in the system prompt

description.description: One-line description shown beside the name (the model decides from this alone)

manual.description: Free-text manual the model pulls on demand: the API shape plus 1-2 curl/shell examples

name.description: Peer name (also keys the NOVACLAW_INSTANCE_<NAME>_* env vars)

url.description: The peer's base URL, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:4097
